declared difference (truth fix T1): the bash awk closed an annotation only from its second line, so a
one-line @NiagaraProperty swallowed the next line and every other one of a run of one-line annotations
went uncounted (it printed N=2 for OneLine, and nothing for Pair). Each one is counted now.
-- args --
@DIR@
-- want --
exit 0
WARN  lint-status-parity  OneLine  N=4 per-instance config slots but 1 status slots
WARN  lint-status-parity  Pair  N=2 per-instance config slots but 0 status slots
-- stderr --
-- OneLine.java --
class OneLine {
  @NiagaraProperty(name = "aInterval", type = "int", defaultValue = "1")
  @NiagaraProperty(name = "bInterval", type = "int", defaultValue = "1")
  @NiagaraProperty(name = "cInterval", type = "int", defaultValue = "1")
  @NiagaraProperty(name = "dInterval", type = "int", defaultValue = "1")
  @NiagaraProperty(name = "xActive", type = "int", defaultValue = "1")
}
-- Pair.java --
class Pair {
  @NiagaraProperty(name = "aSetpoint", type = "double", defaultValue = "1")
  @NiagaraProperty(name = "bSetpoint", type = "double", defaultValue = "1")
}
